Banchan / Heritage

Baechu Geotjeori Fresh Kimchi

Geotjeori is kimchi's answer to right now: napa cabbage salted just enough to soften, dressed in the full kimchi paste, and on the table within the hour — no ferment, no jar, no waiting.

Korean · Easy · Serves 6–8 as banchan

Chapter 03 / 25 banchan recipes ↗

Behind the dish

A PLACE AT
the table.

Stream: heritage — the unfermented same-day kimchi. Geotjeori is kimchi's answer to right now: napa cabbage salted just enough to soften, dressed in the full kimchi paste, and on the table within the hour — no ferment, no jar, no waiting. It is sweeter and greener than the fermented bowl (#B01), built for the day the jar runs empty or the grill was decided this morning. This is also the record for the first-time kimchi maker: every flavor of the tradition, none of the calendar.

The cabbage and salt
The dressing

Set yourself up

Before you cook

  • A short salt, not a brine. Toss the cut cabbage with the salt, rest 20 minutes, and it weeps enough to wilt the leaves a half-step while staying crisp — geotjeori's whole texture. Rinse lightly, squeeze firmly by the handful (squeezing also breaks the leaves' cell walls so the dressing soaks in — this dish's one physical technique), and drain.
  • Build the dressing while the cabbage sits.

LET’S make it.

  1. 01
    Gochugaru, fish sauce, garlic, ginger, and sugar worked to a paste, loosened with a tablespoon of the cabbage's rinse water; pear matchsticks and scallion folded through. Checkpoint — the paste tastes complete and slightly over-strong (sweet-savory-hot with a raw gochugaru edge) — the cabbage's water rounds it within the hour.
  2. 02
    The squeezed cabbage and the dressing tossed together by hand, massaged for a full minute so every leaf's surface takes the paste, sesame oil and seeds last. Checkpoint — the bowl test, ten minutes after mixing: crisp, wet-crunchy leaves, the dressing clinging rather than pooling, the flavor fully arrived — bright, sweet-hot, green. No sourness, and none expected: geotjeori's identity is the absence of the ferment. Chef’s Note — geotjeori is the grill table's flexible kimchi in ways the jar cannot match: it takes variation freely (a handful of sliced cucumber, radish matchsticks, perilla), it can be made at the exact heat the table wants on the exact day, and it is the correct kimchi for the times the meal needs the bowl in one hour rather than one week. The jar (#B01) carries tradition's depth; this bowl carries its convenience — and the honest kitchen keeps both in rotation.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Watery bowl in an hourCabbage under-squeezedHandful-by-handful squeeze before dressing
Dressing slid offDry-leaf tossingThe full minute's massage
Flat, not brightMissing sugar or pearBoth are load-bearing in the fresh build
Went limp by next dayIt kept — it shouldn'tEat within 3 hours; that is the dish's clock

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

  • Best within 3 hours, acceptable at a day refrigerated, wrong at two — this is a make-and-eat bowl.
  • Variations: cucumber-geotjeori (#B03's instant cousin); a spoon of the leftover dressing makes instant radish geotjeori; the fermented commitment is B01.
